summary: An owned-set publication checks only the exec gates of missions whose exact revision the daemon does not hold yet, so publishing or adopting a large set no longer reruns every unchanged member's gates on the publishing daemon

replay.detail: No claim kind or projection change; gate checks never reach the graph.

schema.detail: No table, index or migration change.

rules.detail: No admission or authority change; --no-gate-check and --check keep their meaning.

compatibility.detail: The set preview gains `gate_check`, the mission subjects whose revision this store does not hold yet. A held revision is not checked again, including one published with --no-gate-check or replicated from another daemon; `fractal missions check FILE` checks it. `POST /v1/gate-checks` accepts an optional `missions` subject list that limits the check; a daemon without it checks every mission, as before. `fractal apply --set` checks only `gate_check` and skips the check when it is empty; against an older daemon it checks every mission. Plain `apply` and `missions check` still check every mission.

downtime.detail: No restart or migration beyond a normal deploy.

manual.detail: Set publishers that passed --no-gate-check only to avoid the full-set check can drop the flag once their daemon runs this release.
